topic: Using the Standard Template Library (STL) sort() Algorithm with Iterators
explanation: In modern C++, the STL provides generic algorithms like sort() that operate on ranges defined by iterators. This allows for flexible, efficient, and type-safe sorting of containers such as vectors, lists, or arrays. The sort() algorithm typically implements a variation of quicksort, offering good average-case performance with a complexity of O(n log n). Using iterators, programmers can sort any container that supports iterator access, promoting code reusability and abstraction.
syntax: template <class RandomIt> void sort(RandomIt first, RandomIt last);
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of the STL sort() algorithm to sort a vector of integers. By passing the vector's begin() and end() iterators, the sort() function rearranges the elements into ascending order. This showcases how modern C++ leverages generic algorithms with iterators to perform efficient, type-safe sorting across different container types, emphasizing code reusability and abstraction.
